newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end mixed, spreads fall after easing.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end mixed, spreads fall after easing.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed little changed after a volatile session on Wednesday, with spreads to U.S. bonds reaching 11-year lows, amid a surprise Bank of Canada rate cut, analysts said.

"It's actually been a really volatile day," said David Yu, a fixed-income portfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel Inc. "We've continued to narrow in against the U.S. again. It shows the Canadian market is fairly strong."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.05 to C$108.20 to yield 7.296 percent compared to the U.S. 30-year benchmark which fell 7/32 to yield 6.86 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 44 basis points, the lowest since 1985, from 46 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The Bank of Canada surprised many in the market this morning when it cut its key bank rate to 3.75 percent, bringing the bank's target range for the overnight lending rate down to 3.25-3.75 percent.

Analysts said the cut helped Canadian bonds to outperform U.S. bonds in volatile trading. U.S. bonds strengthened following the release of inflation data this morning, before paring losses to see-saw throughout the session.

In other news, the Bank of Canada said it may increase the pace of its bond purchases in order to reduce its participation in treasury bill tenders. The central bank said it is considering acquiring at auction 15 percent of bonds maturing beyond the three-year benchmark.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.15 to C$102.82 to yield 6.612 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark fell 2/32 to yield 6.56 percent.
The spread reached an 11-year low of two basis points earlier in the session before widening to five basis points. The spread was four basis points at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.40 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.13 percent.
